Sugar is widely regarded as the primary dietary cause of cavities. The World Health Organization identifies free sugars as the essential dietary factor in the development of dental caries [d1]. Some sources explicitly state that sugar is the primary cause of tooth decay [d6]. While bacteria drive the acid production that demineralizes enamel, sugar is consistently described as the essential or primary dietary contributor to cavities [d1,d2,d6,d7,d8].
